**Finding 2 — claim 1 "whereby" clause.** The registration limitation now recites as a positive configured-to element, so the closing wherein clause's "the registered position" has antecedent basis in a limiting clause. Scope is unchanged: the same rib, the same channel, the same closing motion, the same overlap. The description, abstract and figure briefs already recite this relationship in structural terms, so no counterpart edit is needed.

One note from the brief that belongs in the record: no prior-art search was run for this application, so the art considered here may be incomplete.

structured_output.summary: Both verified findings were untraced geometry assertions confined to two figure briefs; I applied the report's filing-clean deletions verbatim. figures/FIG-6.md no longer states that the shallow condensate channel 70 is a recess formed in the upper surface of the shell floor 12 immediately inboard of the shell side wall 14, no longer asserts that the adjacent floor surface is flat and unbroken, and no longer fixes the tray foot 22 position relative to the trough or states non-contact with the channel. figures/FIG-2.md no longer forms the trough within the bottom hatched slab. The channel remains disclosed and renderable as extending around the tray 20, outboard of the tray and inboard of the shell side wall, matching the inventor's "shallow condensate channel around the product tray". No change was needed to the claims, description, summary, drawing descriptions, numeral table, or any other brief: they already describe the channel only as extending around the removable product tray, and the feet only as standing on the shell floor. All numerals listed for FIG-2 and FIG-6 still appear in their edited briefs, so the numeral, leader, and figure-brief synchronization checks are unaffected. No rendered artifact was touched; the drawing pipeline re-renders FIG-2 and FIG-6 from these briefs. As the drafting brief notes, no prior-art search was run and prior_art/INDEX.md lists no documents, so the art considered may be incomplete.
